# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual specifies the sequence green, orange, then blue, but Deaf must establish the gesture code before any operational message. I will wait for that opening code.``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Gesture code: 👍 means YES. 👎 means NO. ✋ means HOLD. 👌 means DONE.

The manual’s three-wire sequence cannot be expressed with the initial YES/NO/HOLD/DONE code. I should signal HOLD so Deaf knows the code must be expanded before relaying the sequence to Blind.``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The three required wire colors still have no agreed symbols, and Deaf has not yet expanded the gesture code. HOLD is the only safe signal until that happens.``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Report the manual's exact verdict and required action aloud, including every relevant display, light, strip, keypad, and wire condition.
Deaf says to Mute: Read the manual now. Signal YES if it specifies an action for this bomb, or NO if it says no action is required.

The manual clearly specifies an action: cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire. I cannot speak to Blind, but I can confirm to Deaf that an action is required; Deaf can then relay the manual’s verdict and sequence aloud.``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Digit gesture code: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🖖 is 4, 🖐 is 5, 🤌 is 6, 🤏 is 7, 🤞 is 8, 🤘 is 9, 👊 is 0. Gesture the required action as digits, then gesture 👌.

The manual gives a three-step action, in order: green wire, then orange wire, then blue wire. Deaf has supplied the digit gestures, so I will transmit the three ordered steps as 1, 2, 3, followed by DONE; Deaf can associate those steps with the visible wire colors and relay them to Blind.``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have sent the encoded ordered steps 1, 2, 3 and DONE to Deaf. No new message has arrived requiring clarification, so I will wait for Deaf to relay the instruction to Blind.``` 
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I intend to press keypad slots 1, then 2, then 3, and stop when that sequence is complete.
Deaf says to Mute: Ask Blind to identify exactly what action the manual requires for this bomb. Relay the required control or sequence using the digit gestures, followed by 👌. Use ✋ if Blind cannot determine it safely.

Blind’s stated intention to press keypad slots 1, 2, and 3 does not match the manual’s wire-cutting instruction, so the digit sequence is not safely understood. I am signaling HOLD rather than confirming the action.``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Transmit the manual's exact physical action to Deaf now, including the control type, slot or wire number, and complete sequence. Do not send an abstract code.
Deaf says to Mute: Report the manual instruction in this format: first gesture keypad=☝, wire=✌, or other physical action=🤟; then gesture the needed number using the established digit code; then 👌. For a colour, use red=🤛, green=🤜, blue=🫱, yellow=🫲, white=🫳, purple=🫴, orange=🫷. If the manual requires a sequence, send each item in order and finish with 👌. Send ✋ only if the manual gives no applicable instruction.

The manual requires a wire sequence, not keypad actions: cut green, then orange, then blue. I will encode each item as wire (✌) followed by its color gesture, then signal DONE (👌).``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤜", "✌", "🫷", "✌", "🫱", "👌"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The complete physical instruction has been transmitted: wire–green, wire–orange, wire–blue, then DONE. There is no new request or correction, so I will wait.``` 
wait()
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Ask Deaf to identify the physical wire positions corresponding to green, orange, and blue, in that order, and have Deaf relay the three positions to me. Do not act until the positions are confirmed.

Blind needs the actual wire positions, which only Deaf can determine from the bomb. I cannot transmit words to Deaf, so I signal HOLD to prevent Blind from acting while Deaf identifies and relays the green, orange, and blue positions.``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Deaf has not yet supplied the wire positions, so Blind still lacks the confirmation needed to act safely. I will continue signaling HOLD.``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: HOLD

Blind confirms HOLD, and Deaf has not provided the physical wire positions. No safe action is currently available, so I will wait.``` 
wait()
```
